The fMRI-NF protocol consisted of four 1 h to 1.15 hr sessions within a 2-week period, totalling a maximum of 14 NF runs of 8.5 min each.

task_description.value: Participants attempted to self-regulate activity in a target region using continuous feedback represented by a rocket video, with rest blocks between activation blocks, followed by a transfer run without feedback.

spans.text: In the activation blocks, the neurofeedback of the target region was represented by a video of a rocket, which the participants were asked to move toward space using any strategy they could.
Each fMRI-NF run consisted of 6 activation blocks of 40 s, separated by a rest block of 30 s.

instructions.value: Participants were asked to move the rocket toward space using any strategy they could; minimal instructions were given.

task_description.value: A choice reaction-time task in which participants responded to left- or right-pointing arrows and inhibited responses on stop-signal trials.

spans.text: It is a choice reaction time task where participants are instructed to respond as fast as they can to arrows pointing left or right.

spans.text: The key dependent variable of interest for this analysis was therefore the post-error reaction time to go signals, i.e. the reaction time to a go stimulus immediately after a stop failure, as this variable reflects the cognitive adjustment to making an error.

description.value: Functional MRI data were acquired for real-time neurofeedback and for the stop task; target ROIs were mapped to individual scans using a T1-weighted structural image and a two-volume EPI localizer image.

spans.text: Two target ROIs (rIFC and lPHG - ROI TAR ) were defined in Talairach space and mapped to the individual participant’s fMRI scans via the T1-weighted structural image and a two-volume EPI localizer image collected at the start of each session.
